definition: The process of identifying and removing duplicate or near-duplicate records from a dataset.
details: Deduplication of training data has been shown to improve language model training efficiency and reduce issues like memorization of specific repeated text, making it a standard preprocessing step for large text corpora.

explainer.lead: Deduplication cleans a dataset by removing repeated or nearly repeated records. For language models, this can make training more efficient and reduce the memorization of text that appears over and over.

tiers.eli5: Imagine your folder contains several copies of the same worksheet. You only need one to study from, so you put the extra copies aside; deduplication does something similar for computer data.
tiers.practitioner: Apply deduplication while preparing text corpora by identifying exact or near-duplicate records and retaining a representative of each group. The matching rule matters: a near-duplicate rule that is too broad can discard genuinely different records, so inspect flagged examples before applying it at scale.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a dataset D and a criterion for judging records duplicate or near-duplicate, deduplication produces D' ⊆ D by retaining selected representatives and removing records judged redundant. Training-data deduplication can improve language-model training efficiency and reduce memorization of specific repeated text. Results depend on the duplicate criterion, especially for near-duplicates, where distinct records may be mistakenly grouped.

explainer.example: A training corpus contains four copies of an article: three are identical, and the fourth has the same body but a different title. Exact matching removes two of the identical copies, while a near-duplicate rule can also flag the differently titled copy, leaving one article instead of four.

usedIn.name: Language model training
usedIn.detail: Repeated training text is removed to improve training efficiency and reduce memorization of specific passages.

usedIn.name: Large text corpus preparation
usedIn.detail: Deduplication is a standard preprocessing step before the corpus is used for training.

explainer.intuition: Repeated records add extra copies of substantially the same information. Keeping a representative instead lets the dataset cover that information without carrying all the redundancy.
howItWorks: Start with the records in the dataset.
Compare records to find exact or near duplicates.
Group records judged to contain the same content.
Keep a representative and remove the redundant copies.
Use the remaining records as the deduplicated dataset.
explainer.whyItMatters: For language models, less repeated training text can improve training efficiency and reduce problems such as memorizing specific repeated passages. It is therefore a standard preprocessing step for large text corpora.
misconceptions: Deduplication is not limited to byte-for-byte matches; it can also address near-duplicate records.
It does not mean deleting every repeated word or phrase; the unit being assessed is the record.
Near-duplicate removal is not automatically safe, because a broad matching rule can treat genuinely different records as duplicates.

diagram.caption: Deduplication identifies redundant records, retains representatives, and produces a cleaned dataset.
